title: Support agent with tools and handoff
summary: An LLM agent that calls tools safely and hands off to people.
prompt: Design a customer support assistant that can look up orders, issue small refunds and change delivery addresses by calling internal APIs, and that hands the conversation to a human agent when it is unsure, the customer asks, or the action is risky.

requirements: Functional: chat with customers, call tools (get order, refund up to a limit, update address), escalate to a human with a summary, let humans take over mid-conversation.
Non-functional: no action without the customer’s identity verified, no refund above policy, every tool call audited, replies within a few seconds, graceful behaviour when a tool or the model is down.
estimation: 200k conversations a day × ~8 turns ≈ 1.6M model calls a day ≈ 20 per second on average.
Each turn may call 0–3 tools, so internal APIs see a similar rate; most are reads.
If 15% escalate, humans handle 30k conversations a day, so deflection rate drives staffing cost.
api: POST /conversations/{id}/messages {text} → streamed reply or a handoff event.
Tool contracts with JSON schemas: getOrder(orderId), refund(orderId, amount, reason, idempotencyKey), updateAddress(orderId, address).
data: conversations(id, customer_id, state: bot|waiting|human|closed, assigned_agent, summary).
messages(conversation_id, seq, role, content, tool_call, tool_result).
audit(tool_call_id, conversation_id, tool, arguments, result, decided_by, at), append-only.
design: An orchestrator runs the loop: build the prompt (policy, tools, history, customer context), call the model, validate any tool call against its schema and policy, execute it, append the result, repeat up to a step limit.
A policy layer outside the model enforces permissions: the customer can only touch their own orders, refunds above a limit or outside policy require human approval.
Handoff: on low confidence, repeated failure, a request for a person or a risky action, the conversation moves to a queue with a generated summary; the bot stops replying while a human owns it.
deepDives: Safe tool calls: the model proposes, code decides. Validate arguments, check authorisation with the verified customer id (never one the model typed), and use idempotency keys so a retried refund is not paid twice.
Evaluation: replay a suite of scripted conversations, checking task success, policy violations and unnecessary escalations. Use an LLM judge for tone only after checking it agrees with human ratings.
Guardrails: classify input for abuse and injection, filter output for personal data and promises the policy does not allow.
Observability: trace each turn with prompt version, model, tools called, latency and cost so regressions can be found.
bottlenecks: Model outages or rate limits: fall back to a smaller model for simple intents, or straight to the human queue.
Slow internal APIs: set timeouts per tool and tell the customer when a lookup failed rather than guessing.
Human queue spikes: show wait times and offer callbacks.
tradeoffs: More autonomy deflects more tickets but raises the cost of mistakes; start with read-only tools and low limits, then widen with evidence.
One general agent is simpler; a router to smaller specialised flows is cheaper, faster and easier to test.
Long histories improve context but cost more; summarise older turns.

rubric.text: Defined which actions the agent may take and their limits.
Described the agent loop with a step limit.
Validated and authorised tool calls in code, outside the model.
Designed handoff triggers and the human takeover state.
Proposed scenario-based evaluation with policy-violation checks.
Planned fallbacks for model and tool failures.
